title: Joining Cab Calloway in Pittsburgh and Cab's three rules
summary: He joined Cab at Pittsburgh's Stanley Theater on February 21; Dizzy warned the show was fixed for a year, and Cab asked only that he be on time, play the music and wear the uniforms; he stayed eleven years.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So then I went on out and joined -- February 21st, I remember, I joined Cab, you know, and he was playing the Stanley Theater out there in Pittsburgh. So I walked in and

there's Dizzy [Wright] on the stand, so I walk up there and he just said, "I didn't think you was coming, because you ain't gonna get nothing to play. What we do over here, we set up a show, and that show goes through for the whole year."
Said, "We set it up for a whole year, and that same show goes, the same numbers, and if you don't have a solo --,"

You don't have one for a year, you know. So he said, "That's the reason I was surprised to see you come." So I said, "Well, I had to come anyway. I had to get out of town. I'm tired of playing with Stuff." I want to take it easy. I ain't drinking no more, and I So I go over there and I'm waiting to see when -- because I heard a lot of things about Cab, how rough he was and everything. But he never did me like that, and the only thing was, he said, "Now, Jonah, I don't care what you hear, nothing you hear on the outside, there's only three things I want you to do, and if you do these three things we'll get along beautifully." He said, "I want you to be on time, play my music and have on the uniforms I give to you." He said, "If you do those three things we'll get along fine." So I decided to do that, and I stayed
